newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK overnight rate rises on light month-end demand.
newsitem.headline: HK overnight rate rises on light month-end demand.

text.p: Hong Kong short-term rates rose on Monday on light month-end demand while longer-date money was unchanged in quiet trading, dealers said.

"Activities focused on overnights with bids slightly more than offers," a European bank dealer said, adding that continued demand for the month-end and year-end should lift short-term money on Tuesday.
The overnight rate rose to five 4-15/16 percent from 4-1/2 3/8 on Friday. Three-month money was unchanged at 5-9/16 7/16.
Government paper largely followed U.S. Treasuries, yielding easier, but trading was thin and featureless, dealers said.
Three-year notes yielded 6.02 percent versus 6.09, seven-year yields eased to 7.01 percent from 7.07 and the 10-year note yielded 7.27 percent versus 7.32.
One-month bill yields rose in line with short-term money, closing the morning at 4.34 percent versus 4.28 at noon on Friday.
